overloadPatches.semanticRole: Throws an error immediately, identified by a numeric error code and an optional description text.

discriminatedBy.note: first arg is a numeric Integer error code

overloadPatches.semanticRole: Given an errorObj, throws a fully-described (optionally deferred) error built from its properties; called with no argument at all, instead throws (in deferred mode) every error currently queued for the calling method/Try block.

discriminatedBy.note: single optional Object arg; omitting it entirely switches to the zero-arg 'flush the deferred error stack' behavior rather than throwing a new error

constraints: If description is omitted in the errorCode form, it defaults to 'Error code errorCode: (host)' in the host application, or 'Error code errorCode: (C00x)' in a component.

errorObj properties: componentSignature (Text, 4-letter source signature; defaults to 'host' for the host database or 'C001', 'C002', ... for components), errCode (Number; defaults to -1), message (Text; may contain {propertyName} placeholders substituted from custom properties on errorObj; if omitted/empty, 4D looks up a description in the database's xliff files under resname 'ERR_{componentSignature}_{errCode}'), deferred (Boolean, default false; when true, the error is deferred until the current method/Try block ends), plus any custom properties referenced by message placeholders.
Errors thrown via throw are handled like any normal 4D error: the standard error dialog appears unless an interception method is installed via ON ERR CALL.
throw can be called multiple times in the same method to queue several errors, typically combined with deferred:true, then flushed together via the zero-argument call.

The zero-argument call is typically made from within an ON ERR CALL callback; queued errors are exposed via the Last errors command, and in a component the error stack can be relayed to the host application's ON ERR CALL.
